title: Lightweight Transformer for Scientific Document Classification
text: Abstract. We propose a lightweight transformer-based approach for scientific document classification. We evaluate on a public dataset of 2,400 abstracts and compare against TF-IDF and a pretrained transformer. The proposed model achieves 4.2% higher macro-F1 than TF-IDF, but only a 0.6% gain over the pretrained transformer. We use a single train-test split and do not report confidence intervals or multiple random seeds. The dataset contains computer science papers from 2019 to 2023. We do not include an ablation study to isolate the contribution of domain-specific embeddings. Methods. The dataset is split into 80% training and 20% testing. We use Adam with learning rate 0.0001 for 10 epochs. Limitations. Our study lacks external validation and ablation analysis.

title: Small-data Neural Classifier for Medical Imaging
text: Abstract. We propose a convolutional neural network architecture for medical image classification on rare pathology scans. The dataset contains 120 biopsy images across two clinical classes. We compare against a single ResNet-18 baseline and report 99.8 percent accuracy on the test set. We do not provide confidence intervals or external cohort validation. Methods. Images are resized to 224x224 and trained with SGD for 50 epochs. Limitations. Lacks external hospital validation and statistical significance testing.

title: Empirical Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation for Academic QA
text: Abstract. This paper evaluates retrieval augmented generation architectures for technical question answering in academic databases. We compare dense vs sparse retrieval across 1,500 scientific queries using a single random seed. We do not perform ablation studies isolating chunk size from re-ranking algorithms. Dataset splits and hyperparameters are partially documented. Results show a 1.2% improvement over standard BM25 retrieval.

title: Attention Sparsification in Vision Transformers for Edge Devices
text: Abstract. We present a dynamic token pruning mechanism for vision transformers deployed on edge microcontrollers. We evaluate on ImageNet-100 with 10,000 samples and demonstrate a 28% reduction in multiply-accumulate operations with only a 0.8% loss in top-1 accuracy. We use 3 random seeds and report mean and standard deviation. Limitations. Does not benchmark on full ImageNet-1k due to compute constraints.
